ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What layer is between layer L and layer C?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a schematic diagram of a plant cell structure, with multiple letter labels on the right and lower right sides. The leader line labeled C points to the thick green boundary region on the outermost side of the cell, namely the cell wall position. The leader line labeled L is located near the internal boundary on the right side of the cell, close to the inner side of the cell wall. A very thin boundary layer can be seen between the two. Reasoning: In plant cells, the thick outer layer is the cell wall; the thin layer closely attached to the inner side of the cell wall and separating the cell interior from the cell wall is the plasma membrane/cell membrane, namely plasma membrane. Therefore, the layer located between L and C is plasma membrane.
